cases.title: Anathula Sudhakar v. P. Buchi Reddy (Dead) by LRs
cases.principle: Explains when an injunction simpliciter may suffice and when a cloud over title or lack of possession may require declaration and/or possession. Discusses proof of possession of agricultural land by actual use and cultivation.
cases.caution: Apply to the pleadings, possession and relief in the specific case; it does not mean every land dispute requires a declaration.

cases.title: Jitendra Singh v. State of Madhya Pradesh
cases.citation: 2021 SCC OnLine SC 802 (verify preferred report citation)
cases.principle: Reiterates that mutation entries are for fiscal purposes and do not themselves confer title; disputed ownership ordinarily requires adjudication by a competent court.
cases.caution: Verify the full judgment, citation and subsequent treatment before citing in pleadings.

cases.title: Balwant Singh v. Daulat Singh
cases.principle: A mutation entry by itself does not extinguish or create title; revenue entries generally serve a fiscal purpose.
cases.caution: Read alongside the relevant succession facts and current state revenue law.

cases.title: Suraj Bhan v. Financial Commissioner
cases.principle: Revenue entries do not, by themselves, decide title to immovable property.
cases.caution: Confirm the precise holding and its relevance to the proceeding before quoting it.

cases.title: Kale v. Deputy Director of Consolidation
cases.principle: Leading authority on family arrangements and when a family settlement may be recognized. Registration depends in part on whether the writing creates/declares rights or merely records a prior arrangement.
cases.caution: Registration and stamp consequences are instrument- and state-specific; examine the exact document.

cases.title: Suraj Lamp & Industries (P) Ltd. v. State of Haryana
cases.principle: Discusses limits of using agreement/GPA/will arrangements as substitutes for a legally effective conveyance of immovable property.
cases.caution: Read the full judgment and later law; distinguish contractual rights from transfer of title.

cases.title: Sawarni v. Inder Kaur
cases.principle: Mutation does not confer title or transfer title; it is principally for fiscal purposes.
cases.caution: Check subsequent statutory amendments and exact facts before relying on it.

guides.title: Threatened forcible dispossession
guides.when: A co-sharer or third party threatens to enter agricultural land, remove a crop or disturb possession.
guides.checklist: Record date, time, exact words and witnesses. Preserve messages/photos/video lawfully. Collect current and prior jamabandi, khasra girdawari, crop/possession evidence, site map and prior complaints. Identify whether the threatener claims a share or title, and note pending partition or court proceedings.
guides.research: Consider civil interim/permanent injunction and, where facts disclose an offence, a police complaint. Check competent forum, possession, co-sharer status, urgency, pleadings and exact relief. A criminal complaint does not decide civil title.
guides.cases: Anathula Sudhakar v. P. Buchi Reddy (2008) 4 SCC 594
guides.warning: A co-sharer's rights and possession can materially change the analysis. Do not treat every entry by a co-sharer as criminal trespass without checking facts and law.

guides.title: Mutation challenged as incorrect
guides.when: A mutation is sanctioned on disputed inheritance, exchange, sale, gift, will or family arrangement.
guides.checklist: Obtain certified mutation order and complete file; mutation application and notices; jamabandi before/after; relevant deed/will; death certificates and family tree; service records; objections and appeal/revision history. Verify limitation only after identifying the governing provision.
guides.research: Separate the revenue-record correction route from a civil title/succession dispute. Identify statutory appeal/revision forum and whether civil adjudication of title is needed.
guides.cases: Jitendra Singh v. State of Madhya Pradesh; Balwant Singh v. Daulat Singh; Suraj Bhan v. Financial Commissioner
guides.warning: Mutation alone generally does not settle title. Verify state-specific revenue procedure and limitation before filing.

guides.title: Partition of joint agricultural land
guides.when: A co-sharer seeks division of joint holdings or disputes mode of partition, shares or forum.
guides.checklist: Collect current and historical jamabandi, khewat/khatauni, khasra numbers and area; establish recorded shares and source of title; list all co-sharers/legal representatives; obtain prior partition applications/orders, tatima/shajra and consolidation records; note possession and exchanges/family settlements.
guides.research: Determine whether the matter is partition of an estate/holding under revenue law or requires civil adjudication of title/share first. Check state amendments, forum, appeal route and consolidation restrictions.
guides.cases: Research state-specific Punjab and Haryana High Court authorities for the exact statute, holding and procedural stage.
guides.warning: Do not assume all co-owner disputes belong in the same forum; title disputes and revenue partition powers must be analysed separately.

guides.title: Proving long-standing possession
guides.when: Parties dispute who cultivated or possessed the land over multiple crop seasons.
guides.checklist: Collect certified khasra girdawari/crop entries, jamabandi, irrigation/electricity or input records where relevant, crop sale receipts, dated photographs with context, independent witnesses, prior proceedings and admissions. Preserve originals and identify official record custodians.
guides.research: Map each factual assertion to admissible evidence. Check applicable evidence statute, certified-copy rules, burden of proof and presumptions for the particular record. Revenue entries are relevant but do not automatically prove title.
guides.cases: Anathula Sudhakar v. P. Buchi Reddy (2008) 4 SCC 594
guides.warning: Evidence of cultivation may support possession but does not by itself necessarily prove ownership. Never alter or retrospectively create records.

guides.title: Suspected forged deed or false record
guides.when: A party suspects a forged deed, fabricated signature, false mutation supporting document or altered record.
guides.checklist: Secure certified copies from registering/revenue authority; preserve the original where available; record document number/date/execution/registration details and custody; compare admitted signatures/specimens through lawful process; note who produced or relied on the document; preserve electronic source data without editing.
guides.research: Assess civil remedies to challenge the instrument/entry and separate criminal complaint options. Identify date of conduct and applicable BNS/IPC and BNSS/CrPC regime under transition provisions. Consider expert opinion where appropriate.
guides.cases: Research document-specific Supreme Court and Punjab and Haryana High Court authorities after identifying the alleged act and procedural stage.
guides.warning: Do not publicly accuse a person of forgery without evidence. Offence sections depend on precise conduct, intent, document and applicable temporal law.

guides.title: Inheritance and succession dispute
guides.when: Land devolves after death and heirs disagree about shares, a will, coparcenary status or family arrangement.
guides.checklist: Prepare family tree with dates of birth/death; obtain death certificates, original will and witnesses if any, registered instruments, earlier jamabandis, mutation file, and records establishing property character and family relationships where relevant.
guides.research: Identify applicable personal law, whether property is coparcenary or separate property, dates relevant to amendments, proof of will, limitation and appropriate civil/revenue forum.
guides.cases: Kale v. Deputy Director of Consolidation (1976) 3 SCC 119 may be relevant to family settlements; identify more specific succession precedents for the facts.
guides.warning: Do not calculate shares from family relationships alone without confirming personal law, property character and relevant dates.
